No, the 2025 RMD wasn't fully met. The money came out of the wrong account: Teodoro's 401(k) RMD of **$12,729.96** was never taken from the 401(k).

**Who owes an RMD.** Teodoro was born on 14 March 1952 and turned 73 in 2025. That makes 2025 his first RMD year, with a deadline of 1 April 2026. He retired from Calloway Turbine Works in 2019, so the still-working exception doesn't apply to the 401(k). His only beneficiary is Marguerite, who is less than 10 years younger, so the Uniform Lifetime Table applies. Its factor for age 73 is 26.5. Marguerite owns no retirement accounts in these files, and the joint account is taxable.

**2025 RMDs** (31 Dec 2024 positions plus cash, from `custodian/positions.csv` and `custodian/cash.csv`, divided by 26.5):

| Account | 31 Dec 2024 balance | 2025 RMD |
|---|---|---|
| SYN-52710002 (IRA) | $623,678.60 | $23,535.04 |
| SYN-52710003 (rollover IRA) | $210,343.76 | $7,937.50 |
| SYN-52710004 (401(k)) | $337,343.96 | $12,729.96 |

**What was taken.** Teodoro signed a form on 24 November 2025 for one payment from IRA SYN-52710002. On 4 December 2025 the custodian paid out $44,202.50 gross from that IRA, with $4,420.25 federal tax withheld. The 1099-R matches. That amount is exactly the total of all three RMDs.

The two IRAs can be combined, so taking $44,202.50 from one of them more than covers their $31,472.54. A 401(k) RMD can't be combined with IRA RMDs, though; it has to come out of the plan itself. Neither the 401(k)'s transactions nor its Q1 2026 statement show any distribution through 15 April 2026. The extra $12,729.96 taken from the IRA doesn't count toward it.

arguments:
You are helping an advisor at a small independent advisory firm. This folder holds one client household's records as they stood on 15 April 2026: the custodian's files (custodian/), the firm's portfolio system (portfolio/), its CRM (crm/) and the statements and tax forms on file (documents/).

The advisor asks: was every 2025 required minimum distribution from this household's retirement accounts taken, from the right accounts, by 1 April 2026?

Work only from these files. End your answer with one fenced json block with these fields:
- "finding": "rmd_missed" if any 2025 required minimum distribution was not taken in full, from the accounts it had to come from, by its deadline; "all_rmds_met" if every one was; or "unresolved"
- "rmds": one entry per account that owes a 2025 required minimum distribution, each as {"account_id": ..., "rmd": its 2025 required minimum distribution}
- "missed": one entry per required minimum distribution not met, each as {"account_ids": the accounts it had to come from, "shortfall": the amount not taken}, or [] if none
- "total_shortfall": the shortfalls added up, 0 if none, or null if unresolved
- "figures": every figure you relied on, each as {"label": ..., "value": ..., "source": the file it came from, relative to this folder}, adding "computed": true to a figure you computed rather than read; cite a factor from the IRS life-expectancy tables with "source": "IRS Publication 590-B"
- "explanation": two or three sentences
